question: How does the six-syllable formula ending in the fifth form combine with the one-syllable visarga-brahman through Rudra's power?
premises: A six-syllable formula ends with the fifth form.
It is pronounced as may-be by Rudra's power.
Then the one-syllable visarga-brahman is declared.
inference: Rudra's power joins the six-syllable formula to the one-syllable brahman.
uncertainties: pañcamyanta may refer to an ablative or ordinal ending.
visargabrahma is not identified further here.
plain_english: The six-syllable formula ending in the fifth form is pronounced as may-be by Rudra's power; then the one-syllable visarga-brahman is declared.
